sections.overview: Scyliorhinus stellaris is a large bottom-dwelling catshark of the northeastern Atlantic and Mediterranean.
sections.identification: Its back bears large, widely spaced dark spots; unlike the smaller Scyliorhinus canicula, it has fewer, larger markings.
sections.habitat: It rests under rocks or in crevices by day and becomes active at night, over hard or rocky seabeds.
sections.diet: Its prey includes crustaceans, molluscs, cephalopods and fishes.
sections.behavior: It is a nocturnal predator that spends daylight hours sheltered on the seabed.
sections.reproduction: Females lay egg cases with long tendrils that catch on sea fans or algae.
sections.ecology: Its egg cases resemble those of Scyliorhinus canicula but are substantially larger.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN Red List assessment classifies the Nursehound as Vulnerable.
